policy: References informed proportions, fin layout, meristics and colour placement only. No pixels were sampled, traced, copied or redistributed. Seller imagery was not used as a texture, proportion or tracing source; trade names (Diamond Goby, Orange-spotted Sleeper Goby) were used for identity only.

sources.title: Valenciennea puellaris species summary: max length 20.0 cm SL; D VII (VI + I), 11-12; A I, 11-12; body depth 4.8-6.0 in SL; rounded caudal fin 3.0-4.2 in SL; 79-91 longitudinal scales; head scaleless; pale grey body with a row of large orange spots on the side, dash-like markings below, smaller orange spots on the back and blue to whitish streaks on the head

Revision of the Indo-Pacific gobiid fish genus Valenciennea, with descriptions of seven new species. Indo-Pacific Fishes 23 (cited through FishBase as the source of the meristic and proportion data used here)

Orangespotted Glidergoby, Valenciennea puellaris species account: light brown to grey above and white below, blue-edged orange line along the lower side, orange dashes on the upper body, two rows of light blue dashes on the head
Orangespotted Glidergoby, Valenciennea puellaris species page (colour description and habits)

taxonomyNote: Identity recorded as the western Pacific Valenciennea puellaris (Tomiyama, 1956); Indian Ocean populations formerly placed here are now treated as a distinct species, so the Pacific colour form (spots and dashes rather than a continuous lower stripe) is the one modelled.
referenceGradeRationale: Meristics, body depth and caudal proportions come from FishBase (Hoese and Larson 1994); openly licensed lateral and oblique photographs are available for proportion study; top and front views are inferred from general Valenciennea and Gobiinae body plans rather than calibrated dorsal photographs.
